raw.details:
Code and Craft is the premier Design & Development competition, where you can showcase your creativity and subject your development skills to bring it to life.

Code it. Craft it. Show it.

Guidelines:

  • Eligibility: Open to students from all colleges and universities
  • Team Size: 1-3 participants per team
  • Inter-College Teams: Allowed. Participants from different colleges may form a team
  • Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed. Participants from differents branches/specializations may form a team.
  • Competition Format: The competition consists of three rounds:
    • Ideate and Create - Design and conceptualization
    • Bring to Life - Website development and implementation
    • Showcase - Live demonstration and Q&A
  • Problem Statements: A theme/problem statement will be provided by the organizers at the beginning of the competition. Teams must develop their solution around the given theme.
  • Design Tools: Participants may use any design tool of their choice; Figma is preferred.
  • Development Tools: Participants may use any suitable technology, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, frameworks, or approved no-code platforms.
  • Submission: All deliverables must be submitted through the official submission portal within the specified deadline.
  • Presentation: Teams must be prepared to explain their ideation, design process, technology choices, implementation, and final product during the showcase.

Rules:

General Rules

  • All work must be original and created from scratch.
  • Templates, copied websites, plagiarized designs, and previously completed projects are not permitted.
  • The final solution must clearly address and reflect the given theme/problem statement.
  • Teams must adhere to the specified team size of 1-3 participants.
  • Participants must submit their work within the specified deadline to qualify for the subsequent round.
  • Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project is functional and ready for demonstration during the showcase.
  • Any form of plagiarism or submission of substantially pre-existing work may result in disqualification.

Round 1 - Ideate and Create

  • Teams must brainstorm and develop their solution based on the given theme/problem statement.
  • Teams must submit wireframes and/or high-fidelity mockups.
  • AI tools may be used only for ideation and brainstorming.
  • AI must not be used to generate the mockups or design assets.
  • The submitted design must be the team's own work.

Round 2 - Bring to Life

  • Teams must develop a working and responsive website based on their submitted design.
  • The website must include at least one meaningful interactive feature, such as an animation, quiz, form, dynamic interaction, or similar functionality.
  • The implementation should maintain consistency with the submitted design.
  • AI tools may be used for website implementation, but the final website must reflect the team's own design decisions.
  • Any technology or development stack may be used, including coding and permitted no-code platforms.

Round 3 - Showcase

  • Teams must provide a live demonstration of their final website.
  • Teams must explain:
    • The initial idea and brainstorming process
    • Problem interpretation
    • Wireframes and mockups
    • Design decisions
    • Team members' contributions
    • Technology/stack selection
    • Development process
    • Interactive features
    • Final implementation
  • Judges may question participants about any stage of the competition.
  • Participants should be able to justify their design and technical decisions.

Tie-Breaker

In case of a tie, design quality, accessibility, usability, and consistency between the submitted design and final implementation will be scrutinized.
